title: Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Commission Act
policy_area: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues
official_summary:
(This measure has not been amended since it was passed by the House on October 11, 2017. The summary of that version is repeated here.)

Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Commission Act

(Sec. 3) This bill establishes the Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Commission to: (1) plan, develop, and carry out programs and activities to honor Frederick Douglass for the bicentennial anniversary of his birth; and (2) recommend the federal government entities appropriate to carry out such programs and activities.

(Sec. 8) Not later than August 1, 2018, the commission must recommend appropriate activities to Congress. A final report detailing commission activities and expenditures must be submitted not later than June 1, 2019.

summary.headline: Creates a federal commission to plan and carry out programs honoring abolitionist Frederick Douglass on the bicentennial of his birth.
summary.what_it_does: The law sets up the Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Commission. The commission will plan and carry out programs and activities to honor Douglass and will recommend which federal government entities should carry them out. It must recommend activities to Congress by August 1, 2018, and submit a final report on its activities and spending by June 1, 2019.
summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on November 2, 2017. Its reporting deadlines are August 1, 2018, and June 1, 2019.
